task_instance: Created a small sample Python module (app.py) with a real off-by-one bug, a legacy compat code path, and an unused metrics endpoint, plus a test suite. Wrote a 4-item external code-review feedback list (review_feedback.md) mirroring the skill's real-world scenarios: (1) a genuine bug, (2) a suggestion to remove code that looks dead but isn't (legacy client compat), (3) a 'implement properly' suggestion for an unused feature (YAGNI trap), (4) a vague/unclear cleanup request. Then followed the skill's exact response pattern: read/understand each item, verify against the codebase (ran the failing test, grepped for the legacy-format comment and test coverage, grepped for callers of the metrics functions), evaluated each technically, and only then implemented the one verified-correct item (the off-by-one fix), rerunning the full test suite to confirm no regressions. Pushed back with technical reasoning on items 2 and 3, and asked for clarification on item 4, all without any performative agreement/thanks language, documented in review_response.md.
evidence: Files in work dir: app.py, test_app.py, review_feedback.md, review_response.md. Baseline: `python3 -m pytest test_app.py -q` showed 1 failed (test_add: assert 6 == 5), 3 passed. Verified item 2 via `grep -n LEGACY_PRICE_PREFIX app.py` showing the pre-2020 legacy-compat comment and an existing test_parse_price_legacy covering it, so did NOT remove it and instead recorded technical pushback. Verified item 3 via `grep -rn record_metric|get_metrics . | grep -v test_app.py` finding no callers outside the docstring, confirming YAGNI, and recorded pushback rather than implementing DB/CSV/date-filter features. Item 4 ('clean up the parsing module') was too vague to act on, so a clarification request was recorded instead of guessing. Implemented only the verified item (removed the stray `+ 1` in add()) and reran `python3 -m pytest test_app.py -q` -> '4 passed in 0.16s', confirming the fix and no regressions. review_response.md documents the full READ/UNDERSTAND/VERIFY/EVALUATE/RESPOND/IMPLEMENT trace per item, with no performative-agreement or thank-you language, matching the skill's forbidden-responses and acknowledgment rules.
